recs.name: Heartfelt Present
recs.tag: The search for truth is far more difficult than she imagined, but she learned to seek the encouragement and support from those who walk the same path.

lines.x: 'A few months ago, when I first entered university, I sent you a postcard of the National University Library.'
'I was ever so excited when I gazed upon the rows and rows of bookshelves rising to the ceiling, and when I listened to the footsteps of my classmates echo through that great building.'
'I thought there was no limit to knowledge held here, and that I could find the answer that I sought—the cure to your disease.'
'But when I stand in the same place today, I find myself in a daze. Each and every step needed to reach the bookshelves has become an arduous trek.'

'I've become afraid of the library, of the laboratories, of the classrooms. I fear giving everything my all like before. Whenever my eyes land on a passage that I cannot follow, I feel more exhausted than ever.'
'I can't help but wonder if the time I have here is enough to learn all that I want to know.'
'What if I exhaust all the knowledge here—like draining dry the Siestan sea—and I still cannot find my answer?'
'What should I do?'
—A discarded letter folded neatly into thirds at the bottom of the rubbish bin.

'Hot Sami-style cinnamon drinks, available only during the holidays! Great for the whole family! Buy two family meals and get one free, plus a chance to draw a special Christmas Messenger surprise toy...'
'The latest styles in the Icefield Messenger series are now in stores! Bringing warmth to your whole family...'
The Christmas sales have already begun? Things are always so lively in the commercial district this time of year.
I don't think I've been to 'Miss Jacqueline's Tea Room' since Schwarz left. Sorry, Miss Jacqueline, but your towers of food are too much for me alone.
The Roxy Department Store is just around the corner, but after visiting it with Schwarz so many times I doubt I could surprise her with any gift I purchase there.

And over there, I should be able to hire an international Messenger directly. The lines are much longer than elsewhere, but I can send out my letter and Christmas cards there. After I buy them, of course.
Hm, I suppose I don't have to write anything on greeting card to Father.
Oh, Rinz! Good afternoon!
Huh? Eh? Good afternoon, Ceylon. Didn't expect to—
(Quietly) Why is she here? What a pain.
Is something the matter?
No, I was just going to say, uh... I didn't expect you to remember my name.
Hm? Do I look like I have such a bad memory? How could I forget when you're the one who taught me to tell Victorian coins apart when we first started university?
Though, aside from payphones and the old vending machines in the hallways, I have to say I haven't found much of an opportunity to use them.
The vending machine was made to accept old coins, but I was trying to use the new ones and it jammed. We only managed to get it fixed because you gave it a good smack.
And then there was the first Thursday Poetry and Tea Party. You were the one who reminded me not to read Williams first because of how famous he is.
I'm not very interested in literature, sorry.

Then I guess you probably remember your report on our last field expedition. The one that included so much detail that it made everyone else on the team look like we didn't contribute anything. Gave us all dreadful marks.
Hm?
Nothing. I'm just saying that I didn't really doubt your memory.
Are you here to shop too?
Yes. Christmas is almost here, so I thought I would buy some presents.
Oh, but this is perfect. You're a local. Would you mind coming shopping with me?
I've been in Victoria for years now, but I normally only visit the large department stores. I'm not very familiar with the small boutiques hidden in the alleys.
Er... me?
Sorry, were you busy with something else?
Right, we do have a few interim reports to write before the Christmas holidays. I'd understand if you aren't in the mood for shopping.
No, no. I'm already half done with my reports.
Please, you're not the only one who does their homework before it's due.
Though, when it comes to experiments, we never have enough time, do we?
*Sigh*...
So what kind of gifts are you looking for? If you really don't want to waste time, we'd better be quick about it.
I don't mind if we take our time window shopping. I need a lot of gifts. We can buy whatever catches our eyes and strikes our fancy. That's how shopping should be.
Huh? I, uh, didn't expect you to have the leisure to stroll around and shop.
I simply feel I need a break today, and Christmas just happens to be the perfect excuse.
...Way to kill the holiday spirit for everyone else.
Never mind. There's a handmade chocolate shop down these steps. Let's start there.
It has twenty kinds of completely different gift boxes, so you can buy all of them and give them out to different people. That ought to simplify your shopping.
Are you listening, Ceylon? Where has your mind drifted off to this time?
Oh, sorry.
You seem rather strange today.
Ladies, would you like to give our new Christmas flavors a try? We have all kinds of gift boxes on sale.
Thanks. We were just about to take a look at some chocolates. Please, tell us more.
Hm... This sample is exquisite! Which flavor would this be?
Raspberry chunks with white chocolate. We have a snowfield-patterned Christmas gift box available, too.
Rinz, look! The packaging is just the color of Viviane's hair! Let's get her this.
Hm... hm?
—Did you just say you're buying Viviane a gift?
That's right. Are you thinking chocolates are too mundane?
No, I'm thinking you two had a row just the other day.
Oh, you mean the argument we had when we discussed Professor Diana's core theories during class? I already apologized to her yesterday.
The professor's Originium experiments already have applications for civilian use, at least according to her 'Originium, Separator, and the Trembling Land' booklet, but I hadn't read it yet.
I mean, it wasn't just the once. You two are at each other's throats every time we meet up as a group.
I took you for mortal enemies.
Is that so? But she's helped me learn me so many new things. I can never thank her enough.
There is so little that we can know on our own. To get closer to the truth, we must find those with different viewpoints and share our perspectives.
Oh, you...
That is probably the main reason I left my hometown to come study in Victoria.
In Siesta, everyone says that the Infected will never be cured. So I decided to leave and see if people from different places and different times had different answers.
Would ancient Victoria know more than young Siesta?
Perhaps.
—Huh? Wait. Infected? Ceylon, you want to cure the Infected?
That's right. Do you think that's too far-fetched?
No wonder you chose to take the pharmaceutical college's courses as an elective, and even put your statement right in the dean's mailbox. It caused quite a ruckus.
The National University's pharmaceutical college is known to be particularly strict. Even if they do accept you as an audit student, they most likely won't give you any certifications.
I'm not interested in the certificates, I just—
—Oh, miss? Hello. Could you help me pick two chocolate gift boxes and ring them up? Thank you.
Of course. Right this way.
*Sigh*... In the end, I never got a chance to chase her away. I even listened to her talk my ear off.
Maybe I should slip away now. If I stay with her any longer, I won't finish what I came here for today.
All ready now. Where should we go next?
...Perfect timing, as always.
Right, just so you know, I'm not going to buy your present today. I'm only shopping for everyone else's.
Huh? You were going to get me a gift? Is our relationship really—
(Quietly) *Sigh* If you knew what I've done, I'm sure you wouldn't think of me as a friend.
After all, how could it be a surprise if I bought it right in front of you?
*Cough*... *cough*! Er, right. That's true.
Okay, please lead the way. Let's head to the next shop.
Hmm... I still haven't yet picked the most important gift, but I don't need to settle on one today. Something so important deserves some careful thought.
Aside from that, all that's left is a greeting card. Once that's done, I'll hire an international Messenger, and my mission for the day will be over.
More international post? You send letters home way too frequently. All those Messengers don't come cheap. Besides, won't you be heading home soon?
It'll take many days for me to arrive. And I think it's better to send cards than to hand them over in person.
That reminds me. How come you haven't bought anything yourself? Have I been getting in the way of your plans? If there are any shops you want to visit, you could bring me along.
It's almost dark. If we take any longer, they'll all be closed.
*Sigh* Fine... Such is my fate.
I want to check out the homeware shop over there. If you aren't interested, you don't have to wait for me.
Homeware? I am very interested!
(Quietly) ...I'd rather you weren't.
Hello, my name is Rinz. I placed an order at your shop yesterday. This is the order code.
Oh, right. Could you wrap it for me, please? This is a gift for someone else.
Absolutely. Here's the item you ordered. Please take a look. Would you like to include a Christmas card?
No, no thanks.
What did you buy?
An automatic teapot. You just need to follow the instructions and put in some water and teabags. It'll keep the water at the right temperature and always make the best possible cup of tea.
I've heard about those! Hm, I wonder what kind of Arts Unit is behind that process? Would it be okay if I opened it up to read the instructions?
*Sigh*. Just take it and do your research. No need to give it back, either.
Huh? I thought you were buying it as a gift?
Uhh...
It's for you.
You can laugh all you want. I didn't expect such a coincidence either.
Pff.
I'd be really happy if you made your tea with this instead of by hand when you have afternoon tea with our classmates from now on. I'm sure they'll be too.
Thank you.
But Christmas is still a month away, and our holidays start in two weeks.
(Takes a deep breath)
This isn't a Christmas present. It's an apology gift.
Huh?
Please don't look at me so confused. It'll only zap what little courage I mustered to do this.
I'm sorry, I was scared to talk to you before.
Er, actually, it isn't just me. Everyone is a little scared of you.
Huh? Why would you be scared of me? ...Is it because I want to cure the Infected?
No, no, of course not! I didn't even know that until you mentioned it today! I just thought that you put in way too much work!
You come from a scorching hot city, but you climb out of bed at six to snatch yourself a seat at the library in the dead of winter! It's almost terrifying how self-disciplined you are!

Remember how we ran into each other in the hallway at ten this morning? I was heading to the canteen for breakfast, and you had a stack of books in your arms. When we greeted each other, I felt like your eyes were saying 'who would wake up at this hour?'
Anyway, your eyes are like an ice-cold mirror. Whenever I see you, I see just how lazy I am reflected back at me.
Do I really seem so cold?
D-Don't get the wrong idea! It's a compliment.
—Right, is it fine if I ask you a question?
Are you perhaps really close friends with an Infected?
Eh?!
...Yes, I am. She's really dear to me.
Is she well?
Her condition has been very stable. Nothing can bring her down. Not even Oripathy.
That's good to hear.
Also, she's not in Victoria, so... the regulations here don't apply to her. If you want to—
No, no. I mean no ill will, and I don't think it's bizarre or anything.
We're Originium researchers. Any of us could one day become infected because of an accident during an experiment or observation. Perhaps even deliberately.
We know what it is, or at least we're closer to knowing than most.
Thank you, Rinz.
*Sigh*. I should be the one thanking you.
Just like you have a dream to cure Oripathy, which led you to come all the way to the Victorian National University, even I have a tiny dream of my own.
I know that all scholars dream of accomplishing what's never been done. I know we'll have to walk this road to the end before forging a new path forward on our own, but... I'm not ready for it yet.
Accomplishing what's never been done...
—Fortunately, I have a fine role model like you around me.
Is that so? Can... Can I really become someone like that?
Just take the compliment. And don't give me that look.
No, please pay it no mind. I just thought of something else... I think I finally realized something.
Oh, and I must insist on returning your gift. We simply didn't know each other well enough. That's nothing to apologize for.
Uh, about that, I hadn't got to the important part yet.
Actually, the reason I wanted to apologize is that I was too scared of talking to you to tell you that the Originium sample we collected from the Catastrophe ground zero had a rare reaction.
What?!
I'm not too confident in my own experimental methods and observations. I kept thinking that maybe it was nothing special and I just didn't recognize it.
But it'd be so embarrassing to ask you to take a look and have you tell me that to my face!
Which is why, even though I knew you would be more interested in its progress than any of us, I didn't dare to tell you—
We need to run! It's only three minutes until the next bus back to the university!
As long as we can sneak inside the laboratory before it closes for the day, we can stay there overnight!
Er, isn't that against the rules? S-Slow down! You're going to rip my arm off!
Master, a letter from Lady Ceylon.
Hm? This one sure took its time to arrive. You were just about to head there to escort her back.
Let me guess: she didn't mention me at all. As always.
Although she has already memorized its entire contents by heart, Schwarz subconsciously looks down at the letter again.

lines.st: 'Since winter began, there has been a fireplace in the library that seems to run on Originium Arts. It's very pleasant to read books there now. My checkout records for this term have gotten so, so long.'

'Ever since I got to know my classmates better, I have gotten a lot of help from them too. Before, I never thought too deeply about it while searching for a cure to Oripathy, but everything that perplexed me has been resolved now.'
'Indeed, I realized how to break the code of Oripathy. Trust me, I will get there very soon.'
'I have attached a card for Father. Please hand it to him.'

lines.x: Aside from the letter, the envelope is empty. The international Messenger's postmark states that this letter was posted three days after it was signed off.
(Lady Ceylon must have been fascinated by something else and forgot about the letter.)
No, Master. She wished you a happy holiday and said she is looking forward to joining you at the dining table on Christmas.

recs.name: The Ones Left Behind
recs.tag: But when someone we love dies, they take part of us with them.

lines.x: Is there really no possibility, director?
You know as well as I do that the remains of the Infected cannot be taken out for a funeral.
What about the ashes?
Even the ashes must be processed to ensure that there is no risk prior to being removed.
We've only recently established this office. The relevant facilities are not yet up to scratch.
How long will it take?
Even if I submitted an application now, it would take at least six months for it to be approved by the landship and for the equipment to arrive.
...Do you realize how cruel this is?
I was both her doctor and her only friend, but I couldn't even be by her side in her final moments.
Then, her remains were quarantined.
And now I need to submit an application just to get her ashes back?
And this will take months?
Please, don't make this difficult.
You know why we have these rules. We wrote some of them together.
I've been working with Rhodes Island for a year now. I'm only asking for this one thing.
I couldn't travel with her when she was alive. The least I can do is take her ashes on a journey, now that she's gone.
It was her final wish.
We're doctors, Hourglass. We have a responsibility to others.
Are we supposed to act like emotionless robots just because we're doctors?!
I don't want to argue with you about this, Hourglass.
I understand that you're grieving. I—
If the day comes when this happens to Schwarz...
Would you still be trying to convince yourself with the same rules?!
You—!
Disposition is about to begin.
Please enter your identification code, then enter the cremation chamber to begin the process.
*Sigh*...
Normally, all dispositions are handled by the office director, meaning me.
If you want, I can let you handle this. Just this once.
...But I'm afraid that's all I can do.
I never got to say goodbye in her last moments. Now I'll never fulfill her final wish. How could I face her now?
...I see.
Dressed in full protective equipment, Ceylon deftly pushes the cart carrying Delia's body towards the cremator.
She has gotten used to seeing and dealing with the bodies of the Infected.
But this does not make it hurt any less.

lines.st: 'If the day comes when this happens to Schwarz...'
'Would you still be trying to convince yourself with the same rules?!'

lines.x: There was clear anger in Hourglass's voice, but Ceylon willingly accepts it.
It is her duty to bear the brunt of such anger. She was prepared for it, ever since she decided to help Rhodes Island establish this office.
As for the question itself—
'It's none of your business what happens between me and Schwarz!'
She almost retorted with that, but of course she could not.
Just as she could not tell Hourglass that 'I understand your pain.'
Regardless of what made Hourglass say it, though, Ceylon had already lost count of how many nights she had spent crying over the possibility.
Every time, she wiped her tears dry, to continue to read the research and write the reports.
It is one of her firm beliefs that tears are less useful than medical research.
If the day comes when it is Schwarz lying on that cart, and it is somebody else pushing it, it could only be because she was prevented from finding a way to save her first.
In which case, she would accept it, she thinks.
She would have done everything she could, she thinks.
I'm sorry, Delia.
Things rarely go the way we want them to.
She pushes the body into the cremator.
After a moment of silence, she presses the button.
...Good night.
What are you looking at?
The sea.
She didn't like the sea. She said she'd gotten sick of it, after seeing it all her life.
She always said she wanted to go on a journey. That she'd go once she'd saved up enough money. But it wasn't meant to be.
You...
I've calmed down now. I'm sorry for shouting like that.
It's alright. I'm glad you understand.
I'll hold a funeral for her in a few days.
Have you already made the arrangements?
Yes. I started planning it long ago.
The ashes were never necessary. I just wanted to give it one last try.
I'm sorry.
You have nothing to apologize for. I know you're hurting too.
But it's hard to keep your cool at a time like this.
Will you come to her funeral?
Of course.
A few days later
The road from Fashion Street to the shore is paved with flowers. Massive flower baskets line the sidewalks.
A temporary stage has been erected at the end of the street, with a dozen chairs set up in front of it.
A photo of Delia hangs high above the stage.
Delia's parents died when she was young. She led a secluded life after contracting Oripathy, but she had a friend who stayed by her side until the very end—Renata.
We'd like to invite Renata to come on stage.
...Excuse me, I have just been informed that Renata is unable to come, but she has prepared an audio recording for us to play.
Huh?
The first time I saw Delia, she was dancing by the seaside. Back then, I hated my life. I hated everything, and was even thinking of letting the sea take me.
But somehow, she seemed to know what was going through my head, and started dancing in front of me.
I will always remember that dance. The way she whirled and leapt across the beach, the way the hem of her dress shone in the sunlight.
These last few days, all I could think of was that dance, the one burned into my memories.
I compiled all my memories of her in an album. I thought that was enough.
I thought I was prepared for the day she would leave us.
But when I woke up from my dreams with a start, only to find once again that she was no longer there, I just couldn't do it anymore.
I miss her so much...
Ceylon feels overwhelmed by emotion. She cannot imagine how she would take it, if the day ever came when it was her turn to experience all this.
Schwarz still has time. Intellectually, she knows that she cannot truly understand what Hourglass is feeling right now.

Yet the fears conjured by her overactive imagination across all those tearful nights begin to overlap with the portrait of pain being painted by Hourglass, prying open the already-fragile barriers of her heart.
She wants to see Hourglass. She wants to talk to her.
Excuse me, sir, do you know where Hourglass... where Renata is?
Er...
Is something the matter?
I'm her supervisor at work. You can trust me.
...She just gave me the recording and left. I don't know where she went.
What?
I'm here, Delia.
In the end, I lied to the director.
She's sharp—it won't fool her for long.
But I don't need much time for this.
It won't take long for me to take you with me, for us to leave this place together, to go far, far away.
I'll take you to all the places we visited together.
And all the places you wanted to go, but never could.
Then, we'll live quietly together, somewhere we can see the sunset.
Hourglass mutters as she searches for Delia's name on the shelf holding the ashes.
She has worked here as a doctor for over a year, and treated many patients. Her hand begins to tremble as she sees familiar name after familiar name.
Finally, she finds Delia's name.
The shelf is a little high. She finds a chair and drags it over. The screeching sound it makes on the floor echoes through the room, making her heart skip a beat.
She steps on the chair. With a trembling hand, she tries to put in the key to open the cabinet with Delia's name on it.
Perhaps her tears have clouded her vision, or perhaps her hand is trembling too much, but she cannot get it in.
She tries once, twice, many times.
Until the tears are all over her face.
Until the key slips from her hand.
Until she falls from the chair after bending down to pick up the key.
Until she is sitting on the ground in a daze.
Until she cannot hold it back anymore, and begins to cry her heart out.
I'm sorry, Delia.
I'm sorry...
It's me. Is Hourglass there?
Director! I thought you asked her to come pick up Delia's ashes?
Where is she?
She just left. Crying.
I need you to—
Hm, that's odd.
Yes? What is it?
Well...
Something was obviously off about her, so I went in to see what was going on.
She didn't take Delia's ashes?
What?
In fact, it looks like she didn't even open the cabinet.
...I'm coming back right now.
How did she do it?
The way she taught me... first a spin, then another—
Ouch!
Look how clumsy I am. I could never dance with the passion that you did.
Hourglass!
How did you find me, director?
You mentioned the beach where you first met her, in your recording.
I immediately knew you must have meant this place. I used to play here all the time.
...I'm sorry.
I stole your pass while you were at the funeral.
That doesn't matter... Well, maybe it does a little. But why?
How do we prepare ourselves for the passing of a loved one?
You've always said you would do everything you can to prevent it.
As for me, I recorded everything about her.
And look what happened.
I haven't had a single night's sleep since she died.
I even broke the rules to steal her ashes.
Why didn't you then?
When I saw the shelf holding her ashes, I realized how meaningless it all was.
It's not her ashes I wanted to take.
She's dead.
All I wanted was to see her one last time. And it made me do something so stupid.
What finally hit me was that—
She's never coming back.
I wasn't ready for that.
How could I be?
Ceylon sits down next to Hourglass.
My father was always busy when I was little. Schwarz was both my bodyguard and my companion.
I liked to sneak out and walk towards the volcano.
I never managed to reach it, though, because Schwarz always stopped me partway.
But there was always something fun, something interesting, at wherever she stopped me.
And so I would enjoy myself there, and follow her home.
I always thought those days would last forever.
Until I learned what Oripathy was.
And so I set my mind to curing her.
To be honest, I'm even more selfish than you.
If there's a chance I can cure her, I will seize it, even if it means sacrificing the time I get to spend with her.
I always thought that, this way, I could console myself when the time comes—that I gave her all the time I could.
But it's just as you said. We were both wrong. All our preparations will mean nothing when our loved ones really leave us.
It was hard enough listening to your recording at the funeral.
If the day really does come when Schwarz leaves me... I would probably take it even worse than you did.
That's how I used to be...
We're all the same, until we truly come face-to-face with the final farewell of death.
Proud, blind. Thinking we can take it.
But when someone we love dies, they take part of us with them.
We can never be whole again.
If... just hypothetically...
If you really did take her ashes... where would you go?
I... I would have traveled with them.
I wanted to take her to all the places we've visited together.
I wanted to take her ashes to all the places we weren't able to.
But... that's just wishful thinking.
...Go. Do it.
Huh?
I said go do it.
I never told anyone that you stole my pass. Officially, you still have my permission to take Delia's ashes.
I'll go back to the landship and submit a formal application for you to go on your journey.
There will a penalty, of course. I'm going to dock your pay for six months.
We also don't have a suitable container in New Siesta yet. While I'm there, I'll ask Engineering to prepare one.
That'll be quicker than waiting for them to send us one.
Wherever you go, however, you must report to the local Rhodes Island office and have your container examined.
If anything dangerous happens, or if I find you spread her ashes anywhere—
You're finished.
Other than that, though, I'll ask them to work with you and allow you to go wherever you want with Delia.
...But there's no point.
I know I said we were wrong. But were we?
We raged against the dying of the light. If parting is inevitable, if we can never be whole again—
Then, at the very least, the traces our loved ones left behind might fill in that hole, little by little.
I'm sorry for acting like I understand what you're going through.
Our situations are different. It's also not my place to order you to do anything. I just thought that, if the day ever comes for me...
I would go everywhere we had left our marks together and cry there. Just like you did.
Once I'd cried my heart out and my tears run dry, then I'd start thinking about what to do next.
But if not even that works...
Then let's get together and talk again.
...Mm-hm.
Thank you, director.
I'm not sure I can be as strong as all that...
But I'll try.
How's my condition, Medic?
A little worse than last year.
You've been pushing yourself too hard these past couple years, both as an instructor and as an operator.
I'll put in a request to reduce your workload.
But my reassignment request—
Would you stop pushing yourself once you get back to New Siesta?
I'll get plenty of rest.
Oh, please. You've been with us for two years now, you think we don't know you?
You'd never take care of yourself, not without someone forcing you to.
Ceylon would've been the best for the job, but with the New Siesta office just getting up and running, it's going to be at least a year before we're comfortable with letting you go back.
But—
Then I'll care for her here on the landship.
Lady Ceylon?!
Hey Ceylon. You're back already?
I was hoping to give Schwarz a little surprise, though.
Oh, did I interrupt you? Apologies.
Okay, take 2!
...I see.
Ahem. Anyway, there's no need to worry, Schwarz. We've come up with the perfect solution for your situation.
Which is—
Ta-da!
And there you go. Soon after you returned, Ceylon made a request to stay on the landship for a while.
Anyway, problem solved. Now I'll give you two some space to catch up.
Lady Ceylon... I thought you were busy in New Siesta.
I talked to Father. He agreed to give the green light for Rhodes Island on certain matters.
They'll be fine without me for a while.
I was doing fine by myself. You didn't need to worry.
Are you sure you weren't thinking about how to hide your condition from me?
Well... no. You would find out anyway.
That's more like it.
Medic was right. You need rest.
So let's go on a trip, Schwarz.
Where to?
You know, I just remembered that you once told me about the city where you were born.
I've never been there.
There's not much left of it.
Then we can leave something behind.
Besides, I know all about your time as mercenary, but you've never told me about your childhood.
...Why, all of a sudden?
I was just thinking... You watched me grow up. You know everything there is to know about me.
But there's still so much about you I don't know. That's not fair, is it?
I'm nothing if not greedy, Schwarz.
I know.
Good. Then let's review your health report, and then we can start planning our trip.
As you wish.
